card.name: Programming text where creating objects comes next
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small linking words in programming documentation where the next word is likely about creating or instantiating an object. Seen after comments, sentence ends, and words like 'be', 'to', 'is'.

modes.label: Code comment before creation
modes.description: A comment marker right before a line that creates an object or window.
modes.example: CWnd wnd;<< //>> Create a window object. wnd.CreateWindow

modes.label: Sentence end in API docs
modes.description: A period or colon ending a sentence in class or library documentation.
modes.example: For a list of all members of this type, see reverse_iterator Members<<. >>Existing Standard Template Library containers also define reverse

modes.label: Linking word before instantiate
modes.description: A small word like be, to or is in a sentence about objects being created or initialized.
modes.example: Unlike classes, structs can<< be>> instantiated without using a new operator.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like instantiate, instantiation and creation.
card.plain: It fires in programming manuals at points where the text is about to talk about creating an object.
